$comment:
Conformance fixtures for the ceremony publication checks. Each case mutates the named base definition and MUST be rejected. Run with `npm run validate-ceremonies -- --test`.

These exist because docs/design-notes/trust-ceremonies.md §7.8 found that the registry's own example validation would not have caught a comparable drift: hex digests sat in published examples contradicting their own schemas while the build stayed green. A checker that has never been shown to fail is not evidence of anything, so the fixtures assert the failures, not just the successes.

`set` writes a JSON Pointer; `delete` removes one. A case passes when validation rejects the mutated definition.

cases.name: exposure understated against the step floor
cases.why: §11 — max() is a lower bound the build enforces; understatement is the failure mode that matters.

cases.name: sideEffects understated against the step floor
cases.why: §11 — unlike exposure, max() IS the value for side effects.

cases.name: prev names a step that does not exist
cases.why: §7.9 step 4 — an unresolvable prev in the definition is a publication error, distinct from an unresolvable prev at verification time, which merely means the verifier lacks a document.

cases.name: prev graph contains a cycle
cases.why: §6.5 — a cyclic graph makes verification non-terminating.

cases.name: no step is marked terminal
cases.why: §7.4 — without a terminal marker every enactment is a prefix and truncation is undetectable.

cases.name: step names a Type URI with no spec in the registry
cases.why: §6.1 — a definition that cannot be resolved to real tasks cannot be enacted.

cases.name: step names a role that does not exist
cases.why: §6.1 — roles are bound at enactment, but the names must resolve at publication.

cases.name: perRole multiplicity on a role with cardinality one
cases.why: §6.1 — fan-out requires the role to bind to a set; this is the check that makes M-of-N well-formed.

cases.name: completion predicate references an unknown step
cases.why: §6.1 — the predicate must be evaluable against the step set alone, with no engine.

cases.name: recorder names a role that does not exist
cases.why: §7.4 — a receipt-level ceremony with an unresolvable recorder can never yield a receipt.

cases.name: evidentiary role used as a step issuer
cases.why: §6.1 — an evidentiary role (the did:webvh witness oracle) signs inside a payload and exchanges no Trust Task document, so it can be neither end of a step.

cases.name: ambiguous deadline origin
cases.why: §9 — maxDuration is measured from the issuedAt of the step that opens the enactment; two required openers leave the deadline undefined.

cases.name: threshold declares both of and ofStep
cases.why: §6.1 — the two threshold shapes are distinct (distinct named steps vs instances of one perRole step) and a predicate must pick one.
